key_insight: On a 3D expansion-compression cone geometry, increasing Reynolds number shifts the hypersonic shock/separation structure downstream, shrinks the separation bubble, and changes the unsteady shear-layer dynamics.
engineering_relevance: These results help predict and manage shock-wave/boundary-layer interactions in hypersonic vehicle forebodies and control-surface geometries where local heating, pressure loads, and flow separation matter.
method: Mach 5 and Mach 8 wind-tunnel experiments on a 7° cone with a hyperbolic expansion corner and 30° compression ramp
High-frequency pressure sensors, high-framerate schlieren, temperature-sensitive paint, shear-stress measurements, and oil-flow visualization
Reynolds number sweep to span laminar, transitional, and turbulent approach boundary-layer states
evidence_signal: The abstract reports consistent multi-instrument observations of shock location, separation-bubble size, shear-layer flapping, and low-frequency breathing across multiple Reynolds-number conditions.
watch_item: Strong relaminarization at Mach 8 limits access to fully turbulent interaction behavior, so the conclusions may not transfer directly to canonical turbulent SWBLI cases.
paper_title: Hypersonic Shock-Wave/Boundary-Layer Interaction on a Three-Dimensional Expansion-Compression Geometry
